# Oblada

> Now in beta: a Chromium web browser with Zen's sidebar, Firefox's containers, and add-ons from both the Chrome Web Store and Firefox Add-ons.

Oblada is a web browser with Zen's sidebar, Firefox's containers, and add-ons from both the Chrome and Firefox stores. Built on Chromium, named after a fish. Oblada is in beta: free, open source, and for now on Macs with Apple Silicon. Linux builds are coming soon, then Windows.

- Latest version: 0.3.0, released 2026-10-22, based on Chromium 156.0.8078.48
- Download for Mac (Apple Silicon): https://github.com/Oblada-Browser/oblada/releases/latest/download/Oblada-silicon.dmg
- Source code (GPL-3.0): https://github.com/Oblada-Browser/oblada

## Features

- **Tabs down the side.** Vertical tabs in a sidebar, with room for long titles and dozens of tabs. The page gets the rest of the window.
- **Workspaces you swipe between.** Keep home, work and the weekend apart, and swipe with two fingers to move between them. Each workspace takes its own color, and can open its new tabs in a container of its own.
- **Two pages, one window.** Drag a tab onto the page to split the view. Drag the handle to swap sides, or onto the sidebar to separate them again.
- **An address bar that floats.** Press ⌘L and the address bar rises over the page like a buoy, with its suggestions right under it. Pick one and it drifts back to the sidebar.
- **Compact mode.** Hide the sidebar and the page gets the whole window. Reach for the left edge and the sidebar slides back in.
- **Containers.** Each container keeps its own cookies, logins and site data. Open the same site in two containers and use two accounts side by side, with nothing seeping from one to the other. Eight colors, the same as Firefox's.
- **Temporary containers.** For one-off visits. Nothing is written to disk, and when the last tab closes the container pops, data and all.
- **Add-ons from two seas.** Install from the Chrome Web Store as usual, or straight from Firefox Add-ons: Oblada converts the .xpi while it installs. Firefox's contextualIdentities API comes along too, so add-ons like Multi-Account Containers work with Oblada's containers.

Oblada's sidebar, workspaces, compact mode and split view follow the design of Zen Browser, an open-source browser built on Firefox by a small team. If you like how Oblada feels, thank the people who thought of it first.

## Installing

Oblada isn't signed by a registered Apple developer or notarized yet. It will be soon: until then, macOS stops it the first time you open it. To let it through:

1. Open the .dmg and drag Oblada to Applications.
2. Open Oblada, and close the warning macOS shows you.
3. Go to System Settings › Privacy & Security, scroll down and click Open Anyway.

If macOS says the app is damaged, run this in Terminal instead:

```sh
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Oblada.app
```

## What's new in 0.3.0

### Added

- Themes for the window: up to three colors in a gradient, how see-through the window is, grain, and light or dark. Right-click the sidebar to edit the default theme, or a workspace to give it its own.
- Three window layouts, in Settings > Oblada or the menu's Window layout: Sidebar, as before; Scaffold, with the tabs as icons on the side and the address bar at the top; and Compact, only the page, the sidebar showing over it when the pointer reaches the window's left edge.
- Settings > Oblada, a page for Oblada's own settings.
- The welcome lets you pick the window layout, each shown at work in a little window.
- Copy Clean Link, in a link's right-click menu and in the address bar's, copies the link without the parameters sites add to track who follows it (utm_source, fbclid and the like), from Firefox's lists, which Oblada keeps up to date from Mozilla. Copy link, in the site's panel, copies the page's link that way too, and Copy Clean Link to Highlight, for selected text, a link to that text.

### Changed

- The workspace's name is no longer shown above its tabs: the workspaces at the bottom of the sidebar tell which one is open. It can be turned back on in Settings > Oblada, where it looks like a heading rather than a tab.
- The address bar shows a container's icon, or a temporary container's number, instead of its name, which hid the address. The name is in the tooltip.
- A container's color mark on a tab sits against the tab's edge, further from its icon.
- In compact mode only the page shows: the sidebar widens over it from the window's left edge, with the window's theme, soon after the pointer gets there.
- In full screen, the bar with the window's buttons shows over the sidebar and the page when the pointer reaches the top, rather than pushing them down.
- The site's information is in the Site and extensions panel, at the end of the address bar, rather than at its start. Sites with warnings still show them there.

### Removed

- Send feedback, which went to Google, is gone from the sidebar's right-click menu.
- Settings no longer has Theme and Customize your toolbar: workspaces have their themes, and the toolbar is the sidebar's.

### Fixed

- The sidebar shows what's behind the window, blurred, instead of a solid gray.
- In compact mode, ⌘L and ⌘T open the address bar over the page, which didn't show.
- Pages opened in a peek work with extensions as in a tab: ad blockers filter them, also once they're made a tab.
- Full screen from a peek (a video's button, for one) makes the page a tab, in full screen. It used to do nothing, and the page couldn't go full screen even once made a tab.
